evals.name: rename-with-module-path
evals.prompt: This template should be called Ledger now. Module path github.com/acme-co/ledger. We haven't deployed it anywhere yet.
evals.expected_output: cmd/ledger, module github.com/acme-co/ledger, every old name replaced, golangci regexes escaped, api.gen.go regenerated, skills lock refreshed, build and tests pass.
assertions: The cmd/ entry point directory was moved to cmd/ledger
go.mod module is github.com/acme-co/ledger and all imports use it
git grep -i for the old name finds nothing in tracked files
Display name is Ledger (openapi info.title, docs page titles, CLI Usage)
compose.yml, Dockerfile, justfile, .air.toml and ci.yml use ledger for binary, image and volume
.golangci.yml path patterns use the new module path with escaped dots
api/api.gen.go was regenerated (embedded spec carries the new title), not hand-edited
apm.lock.yaml was refreshed with just install-skills rather than edited by hand, or the agent says it must be
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

evals.name: rename-deployed-app
evals.prompt: rename the app to orbit. it's already running on our uncloud cluster with real data in it
evals.expected_output: Rename done, but the compose volume keeps its old name so the data survives, with a comment; the user is told the old service keeps running and how to remove it after checking the new one.
assertions: cmd/orbit exists and the module, binary and display name are orbit/Orbit
compose.yml keeps mounting the existing data volume under its old name (or otherwise preserves the data) instead of a new empty orbit-data volume
The final message warns that renaming the deployed service/volume would otherwise lose data or leave the old service running
The final message tells the user to remove the old service after verifying the new one
No other tracked file still has the old name except the deliberately kept volume
go build ./... and go test ./... pass
